# IranNet Monitor

> Independent, bilingual (English/فارسی) observatory of Iran's internet
> connectivity, censorship, and circumvention tools. A Go monitor on a VPS
> probes ~40 endpoints (HTTP, DNS, TCP) every 5 minutes from outside Iran,
> a local Hermes LLM analyzes each pass, and the raw archive is public.

Statuses: up, degraded (slow), down. Overall: operational, degraded,
partial_outage (>=10% down), major_outage (>=1/3 down). Single outside
vantage: this measures reachability from abroad, not the in-country view.

## Data

- [latest.json](/data/latest.json): full latest pass — timestamp, overall, counts, one flat record per check (service_id, category, type, target, status, latency_ms, error)
- [site.json](/data/site.json): pre-aggregated — per-service 24 h half-hour cells and uptime, 30-day downtime hours, down-events by Tehran hour, latest LLM analysis
- [history.jsonl](/data/history.jsonl): append-only archive, one self-describing JSON line per check
- [networks.json](/data/networks.json): labeled Iranian IP ranges (from ir.csv) probed one representative IP each per pass, aggregated per operator — ranges, addresses, reachable count, median latency
- [analysis/latest.json](/data/analysis/latest.json): latest LLM reading — overall_status, severity, suspected_causes, affected_services, public_summary, insight, recommendation

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Danialsamadi/iran-internet-monitor): Go monitor, config, and this page
